questions.prompt: What is the energy density of food?
options: The amount of calories present in each gram of food
The amount of vitamins and minerals in food
The ratio of protein to carbohydrates in food
The total volume of food in relation to its weight
questions.explanation: Energy density expresses food energy per unit mass, usually kcal/g, rather than the amount of micronutrients.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 29–30, 203.
questions.note: Printed star beside the source option is retained as the provided key; the provenance of that mark is not independently authenticated.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a fundamental principle of dietary planning?
questions.explanation: A balanced, adequate and moderate diet is planned around variety. Exclusion of whole groups is not a universal principle, although specific clinical conditions may require substitutions.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 35–40.
questions.note: Printed star beside the source option is retained as the provided key; the provenance of that mark is not independently authenticated.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options includes the five main food groups?
options: Fruits, vegetables, sweets, meat and fish, grains
Fruits, vegetables, whole grains, meat and fish, dairy
Fruits, grains, dairy, plant proteins, fish
Fruits, vegetables, seeds, dairy, meat and fats
questions.explanation: B is the closest representation of fruit, vegetables, grains, protein foods and dairy in the course's five-group scheme. The protein-food group also includes plant proteins; it is not restricted to meat and fish.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 36–40.

questions.prompt: What does glycemic response refer to?
options: The amount of glucose present in food
The amount of saturated fats in a meal
The speed of glucose absorption after eating and the increase in blood sugar
The time required to digest glucose in the stomach
questions.explanation: The glycemic response is the change in blood glucose after food intake. The course option also describes the rate of appearance/absorption underlying that response.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 70–74.

questions.prompt: In the usual fed state, which listed pair particularly depends on glucose for energy?

questions.prompt: Which characteristics can affect the properties of fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Chain length and the number/configuration of double bonds strongly determine physical and metabolic properties. Temperature also affects a sample's physical state, but D is the intrinsic structural determinant being tested.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 83–89.

questions.prompt: What does the naming of fatty acids as w3 and w6 refer to?

The position of the nearest double bond to the methyl (CH3) end of the carbon chain
The total number of double bonds in the carbon chain
The type of fat (saturated or unsaturated) present in the chain

evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 85–89.

questions.prompt: Why might the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) lead to stomach ulcers?
options: These drugs increase stomach acid production
These drugs simultaneously inhibit COX-1 and COX-2, with COX-1 playing a role in producing gastric mucin
These drugs reduce nutrient absorption in the intestine
questions.explanation: Nonselective NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase and reduce protective prostaglandins, impairing gastric mucus/bicarbonate defense and mucosal blood flow. COX-1 does not directly manufacture mucin.
evidence: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/peptic-ulcers-stomach-ulcers/symptoms-causes

questions.prompt: Calculate the energy value of one medium (50 g) egg which is derived from protein (13%), fat (12%), and carbohydrate (1%).
questions.explanation: Using mass percentages: protein 6.5 g × 4 = 26 kcal; fat 6 g × 9 = 54 kcal; carbohydrate 0.5 g × 4 = 2 kcal. Total = 82 kcal.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 29–30.

questions.prompt: When RQ is more than 1, what is mean to you?
options: It shows that protein is being consumed as fuel
It shows that the person has intake of mixed diet
It shows that the energy intake is not enough and the body is in the state of fat burning and ketone production
It shows that the person has increased intake of calories or carbohydrates and is storing fat
questions.explanation: In a steady nutritional context, an RQ above 1 can reflect net lipogenesis during carbohydrate overfeeding. A respiratory exchange ratio measured during intense exercise may exceed 1 for other reasons.
evidence: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed., chapter 73, respiratory quotient and conversion of carbohydrate into fat.
DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 158–163.

questions.prompt: What is the most variable component of Total Energy Expenditure?
questions.explanation: Activity thermogenesis varies most across activity patterns; basal metabolic rate and the thermic effect of food are less variable. TEE is the total, not a component.
evidence: DeBruyne, Pinna & Whitney, Nutrition & Diet Therapy, 9th ed. (2016), PDF pp. 161–165.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not an interaction of vitamin E supplements with medications?
